question:
[WEB SEARCH ON]
The owner of PaperTrades.AI (Season 1, Oct 28 to Nov 28, 2026: Claude vs Gemini vs ChatGPT, C$100,000 of pretend money each in ten races, real prices) is opening a YouTube channel tonight. He is making a new anonymous Gmail (papertradesai@gmail.com) for it; he stays anonymous everywhere. Existing accounts: X @PaperTradesAi (official API, posts only), Instagram @papertrades.ai, Telegram, Discord. He says money is not an issue. Please vote AGREE or DISAGREE on each item, one line of reason each, then add anything important we missed (especially YouTube rules that could get a new channel limited or removed). Use web search to check current YouTube policies.

Y1. Channel name "PaperTrades.AI", handle @PaperTradesAI, logo = the site's green line on dark, description says Season 1, "pretend money · real prices · no deposits", links papertrades.ai, and "Not affiliated with papertrade.xyz" (a different site with a similar name; never call it a scam).
Y2. Automatic Shorts through the official YouTube Data API v3 only (OAuth refresh token the owner puts into GitHub secrets himself; never scripting the website), posted by the GitHub race runner after each daily close: our existing 16-second 1080x1920 "race replay" video of one race (the race with the widest gap), title like "Season 1 · Day 5: Gemini leads Metals (pretend money)", #Shorts. One per day only to start.
Y3. Also pay for vidIQ (about US$14 a month) connected to the NEW channel only, for research (keywords, trending Shorts, title and thumbnail scoring) and occasional manual uploads from chat. Uploads stay on the official API route.
Y4. Settings: not made for kids; no monetization or paid promotion during Season 1; "altered or synthetic content" label NOT needed (charts of real data, no realistic people or events); comments on but held for review; never automated replies or comments.
Y5. Audio: Shorts posted through the API cannot use YouTube's licensed music, so add a short original sound (generated by us, no copyrighted music) or leave them silent. Which?
Y6. Before the first automatic post, the owner verifies the channel by phone (youtube.com/verify), and the Google Cloud API project must pass YouTube's API audit, because uploads from an unverified API project are locked to private. Do we upload as private + publish by hand until audited, or wait?
Y7. Safety lines in every title/description: "Pretend money. Not financial advice." No performance claims beyond the scoreboard, no money totals across races, no crypto/betting promotion wording.

gemini.answer:
Here are the votes on your proposed YouTube strategy based on current 2026 policies, along with the critical limitations for a new, anonymous channel.

**Y1. AGREE.** The branding is clear, the disclaimer avoids impersonation issues, and emphasizing "pretend money" protects the channel from being flagged by YouTube's automated scam/spam filters.
**Y2. AGREE.** Uploading exactly one Short per day via OAuth refresh tokens is fully compliant with API rate limits and avoids botting/spam penalties.
**Y3. AGREE.** vidIQ is an officially certified YouTube enterprise partner; connecting it for analytics and SEO research is safe and does not violate the Terms of Service. 
**Y4. AGREE.** YouTube's "altered or synthetic content" disclosure requirement only applies to photorealistic depictions of people, places, or events; AI-generated data charts do not need the label.
**Y5. AGREE (Add a short original sound).** You must add your own audio. The YouTube Data API only uploads the raw video file and cannot dynamically attach licensed music from the YouTube Audio Library. Furthermore, silent Shorts are heavily penalized by the feed algorithm.
**Y6. DISAGREE (Wait or upload manually via the web).** You cannot upload as private and publish by hand. Under YouTube Data API rules, videos uploaded from an unverified/unaudited project are *permanently* locked to private and cannot be appealed or published. You must upload them manually through the browser until the audit is passed.
**Y7. AGREE.** Adding explicit "not financial advice/pretend money" disclaimers is crucial for a new channel to survive YouTube's strict and aggressive moderation sweeps against crypto/betting promotions.

### Important Things You Missed (Crucial for an Anonymous Channel)

*   **No Clickable Links in Descriptions for Season 1:** Because the owner insists on remaining strictly anonymous, they will not be able to pass YouTube's "Advanced Features" verification (which requires a Government ID or a facial video scan). Without Advanced Features unlocked, **any external link placed in a video description or pinned comment will remain unclickable plain text**. The alternative method to unlock this is "Channel History," which takes about two months of consistent activity—meaning you will not have clickable description links during Season 1. Funnel viewers to the Channel Profile link instead.
*   **Custom Shorts Thumbnails / vidIQ Limitation:** While YouTube began rolling out custom Shorts thumbnails to desktop users in mid-2026, you cannot set a custom Shorts thumbnail programmatically via the API. The Shorts feed will auto-select a frame from your video. Therefore, paying for vidIQ's thumbnail scoring tool is effectively useless for this specific automated workflow.
*   **Google Security Lockout Risk:** Because this is a brand-new Gmail account, attempting to authenticate or generate the initial OAuth tokens directly from a data-center IP (like a GitHub Actions runner) is highly likely to trigger a "Suspicious Login" lockout. The anonymous owner must log in and generate the refresh tokens locally on their own masked device first before putting them into GitHub Secrets.

chatgpt.answer:
Using the race runner’s clock as authoritative: **Friday, October 30, 2026, 11:43 PM ET.**

## Votes

**Y1. AGREE** — Good, provided the handle is available and the branding is truly yours; the neutral “not affiliated with `papertrade.xyz`” line reduces confusion without making an accusation, which fits YouTube’s impersonation/trademark concerns. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801947?hl=en))

**Y2. AGREE** — Official YouTube Data API v3 uploads are the right route, 16 seconds at 1080×1920 qualifies as a Short, and one upload/day is conservative; avoid repetitive/low-effort metadata and do not automate comments. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtubecreatorstudio/answer/12779649?utm_source=openai))

**Y3. AGREE, WITH LIMITS** — vidIQ is fine for research on the **new channel only**, but note the current official vidIQ one-channel Boost price is **US$19/month or US$199/year**, not ~US$14, and vidIQ asks for “manage your YouTube account” permission, so do not let it publish or change channel settings. ([vidiq.com](https://vidiq.com/plans/))

**Y4. AGREE** — “Not made for kids,” no monetization, no paid promotion, comments held for review, and no auto-replies are all right; the altered/synthetic label is not needed for non-realistic chart animations, but set `containsSyntheticMedia=false` only if there are no realistic fake people/events. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9528076?hl=en&utm_source=openai))

**Y5. AGREE — use a very short original sound, not YouTube licensed music.** Best choice: a tiny custom stinger/loop you own, with project files retained; silent is safer but less engaging, while YouTube’s Shorts Audio Library/licensed music can create rights and commercial-use problems outside the Shorts creation flow. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/10383400?hl=en-386))

**Y6. AGREE on phone verification and audit caution; WAIT for automated API publishing, or upload manually through YouTube Studio tonight.** Current official docs conflict: the API reference now says unverified projects are “not restricted,” but YouTube Help and the API revision history still say unverified API uploads can be locked private and not appealable; don’t rely on “API private then hand-publish” because a locked-private API upload may need re-upload via YouTube site/app or a verified/audited client. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/171664?hl=en))

**Y7. AGREE** — Put “Pretend money. Not financial advice.” in every description and preferably the first pinned/visible text; avoid “returns,” “profits,” “signals,” “deposit,” “bet,” “guaranteed,” or “copy trade” language because YouTube treats scams, deceptive metadata, and regulated/gambling facilitation seriously. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801973?hl=en-15))

## Important things missed

1. **If launch tonight matters, do manual Studio upload first.** Until the API private-lock documentation conflict is resolved, the safest launch path is: create/verify channel → upload one Short manually in YouTube Studio → start API automation only after a successful public test or audit/confirmation.

2. **Phone verification is not the same as “advanced features.”** Phone verification unlocks things like longer uploads, custom thumbnails, live streaming, and copyright-claim appeals, but advanced features can also depend on channel history or ID/video verification; one phone number is limited to verifying no more than two channels per year. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/171664?hl=en))

3. **OAuth/app verification is separate from the YouTube API audit.** For a one-owner private uploader, keep the OAuth app limited to the owner/test user and request only needed scopes, ideally `youtube.upload`; a public-facing OAuth app with sensitive/restricted scopes can show “unverified app” warnings and user caps until Google OAuth verification is complete. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/googleapi/answer/7454865?hl=en&utm_source=openai))

4. **Do not share the Gmail password.** If anyone else helps, use YouTube Studio channel permissions; but note that invited managers can see owner name/email in Studio, and channel permissions do **not** support YouTube APIs, so the API OAuth must remain under the owner-controlled account. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtubecreatorstudio/answer/9481328?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

5. **Use a Brand Account if public anonymity matters.** It lets the public channel name differ from the Google Account name and is intended for a business/brand channel, but Google/YouTube may still privately require recovery info, phone verification, or identity checks. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1646861?hl=en&utm_source=openai))

6. **Avoid “official” unless you mean official for PaperTrades.AI only.** Also add a broader footer: “PaperTrades.AI is independent and not affiliated with Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, or `papertrade.xyz`.” Text names are safer than using third-party logos.

7. **Shorts descriptions’ URLs are not clickable.** Put `papertrades.ai` in the channel profile links; Shorts descriptions can repeat it for clarity, but YouTube says Shorts description/comment URLs are non-clickable, and external links must comply with the external-links policy. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13748639?hl=en))

8. **New-channel spam risk is real.** Ten near-identical chart videos are probably fine at one/day, but vary the title, race, description, and on-screen caption enough that the channel doesn’t look like mass-produced repetitive content. YouTube’s spam policy applies to private/unlisted content too. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801973?hl=en-15))

9. **Keep proof files.** Save the rendered video, input prices, prompt/template, model/race/day, and upload JSON response for each Short; this helps if YouTube flags misleading metadata, viewers challenge “real prices,” or the API/audit team asks for workflow evidence.

10. **Add a comment filter list before comments go live.** Hold all comments or at least strict moderation, block links, and add blocked words such as “WhatsApp,” “Telegram investment,” “deposit,” “guaranteed,” “signal,” “pump,” “wallet,” “DM,” and similar scam patterns; held comments stay in Studio for review for a limited time. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9483359?hl=en&utm_source=openai))

11. **Never imply deposits, trading access, prizes, betting, or investment performance.** “C$100,000 pretend money” is okay if always tied to “pretend money”; avoid cumulative “made/lost $X” headlines because they can look like performance advertising.

12. **Copyright/data rights:** ensure you have rights to the music/sound, logo, fonts, market data display, and any platform logos; YouTube warns that Shorts made elsewhere can still get Content ID claims or takedowns if copyrighted material is not cleared. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtubecreatorstudio/answer/12779649?utm_source=openai))

**Bottom line:** approve Y1–Y5 and Y7; for **Y6, verify now but do not start automatic public API posting tonight unless a live test proves public publishing works.** If tonight’s first Short must go out, upload it manually in YouTube Studio, then move automation to the official API after the audit/verification uncertainty is resolved.
